chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I have made upon myself, as gratitude to Allah, two cycles of prayer which I pray in residence and in travel. Shall I pray these two in travel during the day?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.' Then he (peace be upon him) said, 'My father disliked the obligation if a man obligates upon himself.' I said, 'I did not make these two obligatory upon myself for the sake of Allah; rather I made that upon myself to pray these two as gratitude to Allah, and I did not obligate them upon myself. So, can I leave them if I wish?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Can voluntary prayers of gratitude made upon oneself be performed during the day and skipped if desired?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Is'haq ibn Ammar inquires whether self-imposed vows of gratitude (Nadhr al-Shukr) for two rak'ahs can be performed during the day while traveling, to which Imam al-Sadiq (AS) affirms their validity. The Imam clarifies the distinction between a strict obligation (Wajib) and a voluntary vow, noting that since the worshiper made it upon themselves rather than it being divinely mandated, they retain the discretion to omit it if they choose. This highlights the Shia juristic principle that self-imposed vows are generally treated as voluntary acts (Mustahabb) unless specified otherwise, allowing for flexibility in performance and omission.
